results.comment:
Finding stands: the rule equalises the advance box, the ink ends are unequal. Three corrections.
1) The evidence line 'advance-box gaps 4.812-4.814 deg both sides' holds for six words only. NORMATIVE is 3.417 deg and NORMATIVO 2.758 deg each side (tracking floor 1.0). The README states NORMATIVO's 2.76 but not NORMATIVE's 3.42.
2) The first agent's mm figures depend on its measure (extreme ink angle x mid-radius). By true nearest distance the spread is 0.02-0.37 mm, not 0.05-0.19: INFORMATIVO is the outlier at -0.37 mm (8.8 px at 2460; the straight I sits closer to its wall than the round O does), while METACOGNITIVO, CRITICAL and NORMATIVO come out within 0.03 mm.
3) The visible wall is not the plate edge (60/120 or 45/135 deg) but the gold key stems beyond it: 59.079 and 120.944 deg, 44.079 and 135.944 deg (render: 59.10/120.92, 44.10/135.93). The walls themselves are 0.022 deg (0.017 mm) off symmetric; that is included above.

results.title: CRÍTICO's accent sits 0.41 mm from the inner rail
results.measured:
Vector: the accent of the I-acute reaches r 320.3819 against the rail edge at r 317.078 = 3.304 units = 0.4141 mm (4.89 px at 1214, 9.91 px at 2460). On my resvg renders the dark gap between rail and accent is 5.1 px at 1214, 10.3 px at 2460, 20.1 px at 4920 (0.42-0.43 mm), with pure plate colour in the gap: it does not touch.

Every other letter, inner and outer rail: 1.509-1.619 mm (hyphen 3.82 inner / 2.89 outer). Per-word minimum 1.509-1.512 mm outer, 1.523-1.526 mm inner.

The I-acute outline and placement are identical in build 2 (superseded-build-2) and in the owl master (path data plus transform compared for all 8 words: owl equals notation on all; build 2 equals build 3 on all except INFORMATIVO, which replaced NO NORMATIVO).

Other tight gaps I measured in the stamps (letter to letter, mm): NORMATIVE V-E 0.365, I-V 0.414, T-I 0.427; NORMATIVO I-V 0.414, T-I 0.427; accent to its own stem inside the I-acute 0.416.
results.comment:
The measurement stands; two of its framing claims do not.
1) It is the tightest letter-to-rail clearance, but not 'the tightest spot in any stamp'. NORMATIVE's V-E gap is 0.365 mm (8.7 px at 2460), and I-V on NORMATIVE and NORMATIVO is 0.414 mm, the same as the accent gap. Those are the approved track-1.0 legends.
2) The 0.60 mm floor in the build sheet (section 9, check 5) is defined for stroke bridges: ink whose loss would split a letter. It says nothing about gaps. The sheet's only requirement here is that 'the plaque has to fit its accent' (section 8), which it does. So 'under the 0.60 mm floor' compares a gap to a rule written for strokes.
3) The first agent's range '1.51-1.60 mm' is 1.51-1.62 mm by my measure (V, M and N inner clearances are 1.61-1.62).
Scratch: same folder (measure2.py, accent.py; close-ups png/crop-accent-2460x3.png, png/crop-accent-1214x10.png, png/crop-VE-2460x4.png).

critic.verdict:
Build 3 does what the sheet (sections 14-16) and the doorbell (sections 3-5) asked of the build lane, and I found no wrong artwork and no wrong word in any current deliverable. Nothing here is high severity. What is missing sits around the build: (1) the owl SVGs carry the licensed owl vector and the owl README says Hermes "publishes them", against the project's own licence rule; (2) no shirt file has the new stamp or the field; (3) the old owl PNGs are retired by a note only; (4) six README sentences say more than was measured.
